did_you_know.text: The name Yehoshua (Joshua) in Hebrew means "Yahweh saves" — it is linguistically related to the Hebrew name Yeshua/Jesus.
The phrase "every place you set foot" is an ancient way to express a broad land grant, not a precise, map-like border description.
The stretch "from Lebanon to the great river (the Euphrates) and to the Mediterranean" reflects the Bible's largest territorial claim — an ideal boundary, not necessarily actual political control.
The command "be strong and courageous" is repeated several times in the chapter — a clear encouragement for the young leader called to lead a large people.
The verb "hagita" suggests ongoing meditation or recitation; in Jewish tradition this verse is understood as an instruction to study and recite the Torah day and night.
The tribes Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh lived east of the Jordan with their families and livestock — so only the warriors crossed to support their brothers in the west.
